text.p: Belgian non-ferrous metals and minerals company Cie Royale Asturienne des Mines was confident for 1997 despite lower-than-expected lead prices, chairman Jacques van der Schueren said on Monday.

"We made our forecasts for 1997 on the basis of assumptions about the price of lead and the level of the dollar. We have seen that lead is lower than we forecast but our overall, global forecasts are still largely on track thanks to a higher dollar," Schueren told Asturienne's annual shareholders meeting.
Asturienne had banked on a lead price of around $700 a tonne, up from around $640 on Monday, and an average dollar of 32 Belgian francs, up from nearly 36 francs on Monday.
Asturienne reported a favourable start to the year at most of its business units.

Van der Schueren announced Asturienne's 100-percent owned U.S. mica unit Cogebi Inc was close to buying a 60 percent stake in a joint venture company in Shanghai, China, producing mica products for the electricity industry.
"(1997) will see Cogebi strengthen its international position, which should enable it to better resist European and Asian competition," the company said in its annual report.

Van der Schueren said talks in the U.S. aimed at buying a U.S. mica-processing company had run into difficulties during the due-diligence period. The deal was likely to be called off. If this was the case, shareholders would be notified separately.

In industrial minerals Asturienne further restructured its Denain Anzin Mineraux (DAM) unit, buying a 95 percent interest in newly merged Portuguese kaolin and sand company Saibrais-Cauliminas for around 150 million Belgian francs.
The stake was bought from Asturienne's main shareholder, France's La Continentale d'Entreprises , for around 150 million francs.
Asturienne is 59.1 percent owned by La Continentale, itself part of Switzerland's Harwanne Group.

Over the next three years sales at the new unit should rise by 25 percent to 125 million francs and earnings reach 25 million francs compared to a 10 million franc loss in 1996, DAM chairman and chief executive officer Marc Lebrun said.

DAM increased its interest in French feldspar company Etablissements Baux to 100 percent from 30 percent for around 150 million francs, van der Schueren said, making it Europe's second largest producer.

The outlook for its lead and silver mines in Morocco was mixed, with reserves at Compagnie Miniere de Touissit (CMT) steadily depleting. However, overall production of concentrates would be stable thanks to better than expected results at the new Tighza mine, which started operations in May 1996.
In the first quarter of 1997 CMT was on budget despite lower lead and silver prices thanks to the stronger dollar, Asturienne board member Fabienne Herlaut said.
Tighza's reserves were larger than expected and production costs lower, while the proportion of silver concentrate in ore was around 30 percent compared with 10 percent at CMT, she said.
Tighza should produce around 26,000 tonnes of concentrate in 1997, up from 11,792 tonnes of concentrates in 1996 or 15 percent of CMT's total production of 77,195 tonnes.
CMT was examining how to invest cash of around 800 million francs, now held in treasury bills, in mining projects in Morocco or elsewhere.
Van der Schueren said Asturienne was partly financing investments from its 1.2 billion franc credit facility agreed with a consortium of banks at the beginning of 1995.
